introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2024. Additional Mathematics 2 (code 0575), Paper 2. Duration: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions, questions 1 to 8). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions, questions 9 to 11; if this section is chosen, Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (answer any two questions, questions 12 to 14; if this section is chosen, Section B may not be chosen). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators and Formulae Booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

Q12 : les classes 5-9, 10-14, ... sont traitees comme des classes de poids continues de limites reelles 4,5-9,5 ; 9,5-14,5 ; etc. (convention usuelle pour des mesures arrondies au kg).

Regles de choix : la consigne imprimee est « Section A obligatoire, puis DEUX questions de la Section B OU DEUX de la Section C, jamais un melange des trois ». Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks » ; total 66 + 17 + 17 = 100).
Le sujet est une photo numerisee (CamScanner) : texte lu en image page par page ; les filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ont ete ignores.

questions.enonce_markdown:
12. The quantity of maize, in kilogrammes (kg), harvested by $100$ farmers are recorded as follows:

| Maize (kg) | 5-9 | 10-14 | 15-19 | 20-24 | 25-29 | 30-34 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of farmers ($f$) | 2 | 29 | 37 | 16 | 14 | 2 |

(i) (a) Draw a cumulative frequency graph of the distribution. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The classes are measured to the nearest kg, so the real class boundaries are $4.5,\,9.5,\,14.5,\,19.5,\,24.5,\,29.5,\,34.5$. Plot each cumulative frequency against the **upper class boundary**.

| Upper boundary (kg) | $4.5$ | $9.5$ | $14.5$ | $19.5$ | $24.5$ | $29.5$ | $34.5$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | $0$ | $2$ | $31$ | $68$ | $84$ | $98$ | $100$ |

(Running totals: $2$; $2+29=31$; $31+37=68$; $68+16=84$; $84+14=98$; $98+2=100$.)

**Drawing.** Put the maize in kg on the horizontal axis (for example $2$ cm for $5$ kg, from $0$ to $35$ kg) and the cumulative frequency on the vertical axis ($0$ to $100$, for example $1$ cm for $10$ farmers). Plot the seven points above and join them with a smooth S-shaped curve (the ogive), starting at $(4.5,0)$ and ending at $(34.5,100)$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
From your graph above, estimate

(i)(b) the median. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median is the value at cumulative frequency $\dfrac{100}{2}=50$. Draw a horizontal line from $50$ on the vertical axis to the curve, then down to the maize axis.

The point $50$ lies in the class with boundaries $14.5$ to $19.5$ (cumulative frequencies $31$ to $68$). By linear interpolation:

$$\text{median}\approx14.5+\frac{50-31}{37}\times5=14.5+2.57\approx17.1.$$

**Answer: median $\approx17.1$ kg** (reading from the graph gives about $17$ kg).

The semi-interquartile range is $\dfrac12(Q_3-Q_1)$, where $Q_1$ is at cumulative frequency $25$ and $Q_3$ at $75$.

- $Q_1$ (cumulative frequency $25$) lies in the class $9.5$ to $14.5$ (cumulative frequencies $2$ to $31$): $Q_1\approx9.5+\dfrac{25-2}{29}\times5\approx13.47$.
- $Q_3$ (cumulative frequency $75$) lies in the class $19.5$ to $24.5$ (cumulative frequencies $68$ to $84$): $Q_3\approx19.5+\dfrac{75-68}{16}\times5\approx21.69$.

$$\text{semi-interquartile range}=\frac{21.69-13.47}{2}=\frac{8.22}{2}\approx4.11.$$

**Answer: semi-interquartile range $\approx4.1$ kg** ($Q_1\approx13.5$, $Q_3\approx21.7$).
